question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation With Rearranging
question.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T$, where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2y-5z+x \\ z-y+3x \\ -z-2x+3y\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, rewrite the order of the variables in the usual way:

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}]
$$

We require a $3\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x+2y-5z \\ 3x-y+z \\ -2x+3y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -5 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
